newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: EU leaders begin summit on currency, reform.
newsitem.headline: EU leaders begin summit on currency, reform.

text.p: European Union leaders opened a two-day summit on Friday to discuss the path to a single European currency in 1999 and proposals for closer cooperation in foreign, defence, interior and justice affairs.
The meeting began at Dublin Castle only hours after EU finance ministers came close to agreement on a budget discipline pact to ensure countries that join the euro respect strict deficit limits.

The leaders were due to discuss their compromise proposal for a stability pact, designed to prevent overspending, at their first working session after a brief meeting with European Parliament president Klaus Haensch.

They were also due to review agreements on the legal status of the future single currency, and on the link between the euro and currencies of EU member states which do not initially join monetary union.
They were expected to endorse Dutch central bank governor Wim Duisenberg as president of the future independent European Central Bank, in charge of monetary policy for the euro.

The other main item on the summit agenda was reform of EU institutions to boost cooperation in foreign affairs, defence and internal security and ensure prepare the Union to receive former communist central and east European countries expected to join over the next decade.
